chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu al-Jahm, from Abu Khadija, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'How far is it between you and Basra?' I said: 'Five days by water if the wind is favorable, and eight days by land, or something like that.' He said: 'This is not near. Visit each other frequently, and look out for one another, for on the Day of Resurrection it is inevitable that every person will bring a witness who testifies for him regarding his religion.' And he said: 'When a Muslim sees his brother, it is a revival for his religion if he mentions Allah, the Exalted and Mighty.'

key_terms.يَتَعَاهَدُ: Look out for one another / mutual care

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting a Muslim brother according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the proximity of Basra to illustrate that physical distance is no excuse for neglecting *ziyarah* (visiting), emphasizing that mutual care among believers is a prerequisite for divine witness on the Day of Judgment. This tradition highlights the Shia concept of *al-wala' wa al-barra* (affiliation and disavowal), where social bonds serve as tangible evidence of one's faith, effectively reviving the soul through the remembrance of God.

en.hubeali: H 14944 – A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Al-Jaham, from Abu Khadija who said:

Abu Abdullahasws said to me; ‘How much (distance is there) between you and Al-Basra?’ I said, ‘It is five (days) by the water (sea) if the wind is good, and upon the back (of the earth) eight days or approximate to that’. So heasws said: ‘This is not near. Visit each other frequently for there will not be an escape on the Day of Judgement from each human being to bring a witness who would testify for him upon his Religion’. And said: ‘If a Muslims sees his brother, it is a revival for his Religion if he Mentions Allahazwj (during their meeting)’.
en.sarwar: 497. Ali Bin Ibrahiim, from his father, from Hammaad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e, who has narrated the following:

Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said; ‘By Allah (azwj)! No one from the Arabs or the non-Arabs loves us (a.s.) except the people of noble houses, and the (noble) origins; and no one from these ones and those ones hates us (a.s.) except for all the filthy ones and of illegitimate origin’.
